question.explanation:
To compute \[ \dfrac {9v^2+3v} {v + 9} \div {(3v+1)}, \]

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac {9v^2+3v} {v + 9} \div {(3v+1)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {9v^2+3v} {v + 9} \cdot \dfrac {1} {(3v+1)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {3v(3v +1)} {v + 9} \cdot \dfrac {1} {(3v + 1)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {3v\cancel{(3v +1)}} {(v + 9)} \cdot \dfrac {1} {\cancel{(3v +1)}} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {3v} {v + 9} \end{align}

example.title: Dividing Rational Expressions and Simplifying the Result by Factoring

question.explanation:
Since $\dfrac {24a^3b^2} {25c^3} \cdot X=\dfrac {12ab^3} {15c},$ we have \[ X = \dfrac {12ab^3} {15c} \div\dfrac {24a^3b^2} {25c^3}. \]

To compute this quotient, we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac {12ab^3} {15c} \div\dfrac {24a^3b^2} {25c^3} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {12ab^3} {15c} \cdot \dfrac {25c^3} {24a^3b^2} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {12\cdot ab^2 \cdot b} {3\cdot 5c} \cdot \dfrac {5 \cdot 5c\cdot c^2} {12 \cdot 2a^2 \cdot ab^2} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {\cancel{12} \cdot \cancel{ab^2} \cdot b} {3\cdot \cancel{5c}} \cdot \dfrac {5 \cdot \cancel{5c} \cdot c^2} {\cancel{12} \cdot 2a^2 \cdot \cancel{ab^2} } &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {b} {3} \cdot \dfrac {5c^2} {2a^2} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {5bc^2} {6a^2} \end{align}

example.title: Dividing Rational Expressions with Multiple Common Factors

question.explanation:
Since $\dfrac {2(k+2)} {121y} \cdot Y=\dfrac{4(k+2)^2} {11y^3},$ we have \[ Y = \dfrac{4(k+2)^2} {11y^3} \div \dfrac {2(k+2)} {121y}. \]

To compute this quotient, we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac{4(k+2)^2} {11y^3} \div \dfrac {2(k+2)} {121y} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{4(k+2)^2} {11y^3} \cdot \dfrac {121y} {2(k+2)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{2 \cdot 2(k+2) \cdot (k+2)} {11y \cdot y^2} \cdot \dfrac {11 \cdot 11y} {2(k+2)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{2 \cdot \cancel{2(k+2)}\cdot (k+2)}{\cancel{11y} \cdot y^2} \cdot \dfrac {11 \cdot \cancel{11y}}{\cancel{2(k+2)}} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {2(k+2)} {y^2} \cdot 11 &= \\[5pt] \dfrac {22(k+2)} {y^2} \end{align}
